title: Orders and liens recorded after the City bought or financed a building
question: Once the City owned a building, or had lent on it, did City inspectors or utilities still record orders or liens against it?
finding: 13 buildings carry orders of abatement or City liens recorded after the City's deed, loan or lease; 11 orders in all. 4 have Fire Department orders, among them 1000 Sutter Street / 1000 Sutter Street (Hotel Granada) (4 order of abatement (Fire Department)); 921 Howard Street (3 City lien (Public Utilities (water)); 2 order of abatement (Fire Department); 1 order of abatement (Building Inspection)); 440 Geary Street (3 City lien (Public Health); 1 order of abatement (Fire Department); 1 City lien (Public Utilities (water))). Several liens are the City's water utility liening buildings the City itself owns.
how: For each printed parcel, the first document that put City money or title on it (deed to the City, City deed of trust, declaration, lease or security notice; or the Housing Accelerator Fund's) and every order of abatement or notice of lien recorded after it, releases and revocations left out. Mechanic's liens are left out here.
limits: An order records a code violation the owner must fix; many are lifted within months and the index shows a later release only where one was recorded. A water lien against a City-owned building usually means an operator or tenant's bill went unpaid, not that the City lost money. The party shown is the owner of record, who may be a nonprofit's partnership rather than the operator.
